title: How do trees send signals to one another?
sources: Nature Wood Wide Web Mycorrhizal Fungi
University of British Columbia Forest Ecology

lines.text: Did you know that forests are not just silent trees, but an interconnected living biological internet?
lines.caps: Did you know trees *talk | to each other *underground?

lines.text: Ecologists call it the Wood Wide Web, and it operates beneath your feet.
lines.caps: Ecologists call it the *Wood Wide Web | beneath your *boots

lines.text: Trees connect their root tips to an expansive underground network of fungal threads called mycorrhizal fungi.
lines.caps: Roots connect to *fungal mycelium | spanning entire *forests

lines.text: Through these fungal internet cables, older mother trees nourish shaded saplings with sugars and carbon.
lines.caps: Mother trees send *carbon | and nutrients to baby *saplings

lines.text: When a tree is attacked by beetles, it sends chemical distress warning signals through the network.
lines.caps: Sends distress signals when *attacked | by insect *pests!

lines.text: Neighboring trees receive the warning and immediately ramp up protective tannins in their leaves.
lines.caps: Neighbors raise *defensive tannins | before bugs even *arrive

lines.text: A forest is not a competition; it is a collaborative superorganism.
